cells.tense: The sense of what is fair is coming through clean here, and the endings it points at are getting done.
cells.ask: Say one plain sentence to someone about a thing that is ending — no case built around it — then leave the quiet afterward alone.
cells.core:
Something is ending and the weighing of it is coming through clean. You are not arguing with what is in front of you and not dressing it up either. Endings get treated as endings — named, held, let to finish. "Endings honored, renewal trusted" is the shape that holds here, and it is holding without much effort from you.

What it costs to keep: it has to keep being said plainly, and the plain version is the harder one. The line runs against making the ending into something it is not, on either side — not a catastrophe, not nothing. Fairness does not arrive as a verdict; it comes as a right next step. Say the endings out loud as they come and the clearing stays clean.

cells.verb: weighing what is fair against what is

cells.tense: You are running the fairness of endings that have not happened yet, ahead of any of it being here.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you're already calling ended and leave it open for a day — no rehearsing what you'll say, no checking who's to blame for it.
cells.core:
You are already tallying endings that have not arrived. Each one gets scored before it happens, held up against what is owed, redone in your head a few times — and the tallying has replaced the ending itself. The fairness check runs in the background even on days when nothing has actually been decided.

What is being spent is the thing that would carry you through the change. Fairness flows when it is not being guarded; guarding is where all the weight is going right now. The ending has to happen before fairness can be settled about it — not the other way around. Leave one of them open and see that nothing falls over. Then the next one can be met when it is actually here.

cells.tense: The reading stopped at some door behind you, and you are still standing where it closed.
cells.ask: Write one ending you've been treating as still open, then read it aloud to someone who'll listen without stepping in.
cells.core:
A thing ends and it gets named close to when it happens — said plainly, answered plainly, and what comes after met as it comes. The weighings land and the endings get done in their own time, without much carrying around.

The saying has stopped. Endings that could be named sit unnamed, and the reckoning stays half-open, so you keep standing at a door that already closed. The instinct is not gone. The act of putting it into words is. Put one ending in front of someone who will hear it without fixing it, and let the sentence be short.

cells.tense: The reading is happening and you are describing it as the situation reading itself.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've called obviously over — a role, a plan, a tie — and say plainly that the calling was yours, without a backstory.
cells.core:
A call gets made and owned in the same breath. You weigh what is fair, decide, and say it was your call, and the people around you can work with that because nothing is hidden behind the arrangement.

The steering is already real — which favor you take, which excuse you accept, what you let pass — and it gets voiced as if the facts had made the call. "Well, that's how things turned out." "It's what anyone would do." The picture is intact and something is missing from it. Take one thing you've written down as obvious and say it plain — that you made the call. If the situation made it, you're off the hook. If you made it, you have a compass.
